   263	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   264	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   265	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   266	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   267	-/
   268	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   269	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   270	  let lineEdges :=
   271	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   272	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   273	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   277	  let basisEdges :=
   278	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   279	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   280	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   281	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   282	  let pairEdges :=
   283	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   284	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   285	  let msEdges' :=
   286	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   287	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   288	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   289	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   290	
   291	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   292	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   293	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   294	-/
   295	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   296	
   297	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   298	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   299	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   302	-/
   303	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   304	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   305	
   306	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   307	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   308	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   309	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   310	-/
   311	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   312	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   313	  simp [pauliEdges]
   314	
   315	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   316	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   317	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   318	-/
   319	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   320	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   321	  by
   322	    classical
   323	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   324	    exact
   325	      Distribution.map
   326	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   327	        (fun s =>
   328	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   329	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   330	
   331	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   332	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   333	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   334	-/
   335	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   336	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   337	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   338	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   339	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   340	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   341	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   342	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   343	  deriving DecidableEq
   344	
   345	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   346	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   347	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   348	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   349	-/
   350	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   351	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   352	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   353	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   354	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   355	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   356	
   357	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   358	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   359	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   360	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   361	-/
   362	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   363	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   364	  toFun
   365	    | .value a => .inl a
   366	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   367	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   368	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   369	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   370	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   371	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   372	  invFun
   373	    | .inl a => .value a
   374	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   375	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   376	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   377	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   378	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   379	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   380	  left_inv := by
   381	    intro x
   382	    cases x <;> rfl
   383	  right_inv := by
   384	    intro x
   385	    cases x with
   386	    | inl a => rfl
   387	    | inr x =>
   388	        cases x with
   389	        | inl a => rfl
   390	        | inr x =>
   391	            cases x with
   392	            | inl a => rfl
   393	            | inr x =>
   394	                cases x with
   395	                | inl a => rfl
   396	                | inr x =>
   397	                    cases x with
   398	                    | inl a => rfl
   399	                    | inr x =>
   400	                        cases x with
   401	                        | inl a => rfl
   402	                        | inr a => rfl
   403	
   404	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   405	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm
   406	
   407	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   408	  ⟨.bit 0⟩
   409	
   410	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   411	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   412	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   413	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   414	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   415	-/
   416	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   417	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   418	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   419	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   420	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   421	
   422	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   423	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   424	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   425	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   426	-/
   427	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   428	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   429	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   430	
   431	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   432	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   433	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   434	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   435	-/
   436	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   437	  match t, a with
   438	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   439	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   440	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   441	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   442	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   443	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   444	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   445	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   446	  | _, _ => false
   447	
   448	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   449	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   450	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   451	-/
   452	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   453	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   454	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   455	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   456	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   457	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   458	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   459	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   460	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   461	
   462	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   463	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   464	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   465	-/
   466	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   467	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   468	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   469	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   470	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   471	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   472	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   473	
   474	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   475	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   476	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   477	-/
   478	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   479	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   480	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   481	
   482	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   483	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   484	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   485	-/
   486	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   487	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   488	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   489	    (match W with
   490	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   491	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   492	
   493	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   494	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   495	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   496	-/
   497	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   498	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   499	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   500	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   501	      (a * (match W with
   502	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   503	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   504	
   505	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   506	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   507	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   508	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   509	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   510	-/
   511	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   512	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   513	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   514	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   515	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   516	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   517	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   518	
   519	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   520	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   521	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   522	-/
   523	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   524	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   525	  open Classical in
   526	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   527	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   528	      if tA = tB then
   529	        decide (a = b)
   530	      else
   531	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   532	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   533	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   534	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   535	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   536	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   538	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   539	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   540	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   541	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   542	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   543	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   544	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   545	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   546	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   547	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   548	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   550	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   552	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   553	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   554	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   555	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   556	          else true
   557	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   567	    else false
   568	
   569	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   570	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   571	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   572	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   573	-/
   574	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   575	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   576	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   577	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   578	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   579	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   580	  μ_prob := by sorry
   581	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   582	
   583	end

    30	/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
    31	uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
    32	self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
    33	is `def:admissible` in

    37	structure AdmissibleParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q

    45	/-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in

   460	      evalCoefficient f t = a

   462	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   463	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   464	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   465	-/
   466	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   467	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   468	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   469	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   470	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   471	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   472	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   473	
   474	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   475	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   476	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   477	-/
   478	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   479	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   480	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   481	
   482	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   483	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   484	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   485	-/
   486	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   487	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   488	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   489	    (match W with
   490	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   491	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   492	
   493	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   494	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   495	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   496	-/
   497	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   498	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   499	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   500	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   501	      (a * (match W with
   502	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   503	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   504	
   505	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   506	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   507	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   508	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   509	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   510	-/
   511	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   512	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   513	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   514	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   515	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   516	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   517	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   518	
   519	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   520	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   521	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   522	-/
   523	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   524	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   525	  open Classical in
   526	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   527	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   528	      if tA = tB then
   529	        decide (a = b)
   530	      else
   531	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   532	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   533	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   534	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   535	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   536	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   538	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   539	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   540	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   541	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   542	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   543	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   544	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   545	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   546	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   547	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   548	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   550	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   552	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   553	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   554	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   555	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   556	          else true
   557	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   567	    else false
   568	
   569	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   570	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   571	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   572	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   573	-/
   574	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   575	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   576	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   577	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   578	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   579	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   580	  μ_prob := by sorry
   581	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   582	
   583	end
   584	
   585	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Pauli basis test soundness
     5	
     6	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
     7	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
     8	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
     9	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    16	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    30	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    31	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    32	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    33	-/
    34	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    35	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    36	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    37	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    38	
    39	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
    40	Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
    41	matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
    42	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    44	-/
    45	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    47	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    48	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    49	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    50	  U * M * Uᴴ
    51	
    52	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
    53	coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
    54	state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),
    55	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
    56	-/
    57	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    58	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    59	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    60	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    61	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    62	
    63	/-- Coordinate tensoring of two local maps on a bipartite state.  The formula
    64	is a genuine finite sum over the input coordinates; preservation of the norm
    65	is part of the later soundness proof for `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    66	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    68	-/
    69	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    70	    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    72	    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    73	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    74	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    75	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))
    76	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    77	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
    78	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm
    79	    (fun p =>
    80	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    81	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × R) ℂ)
    82	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    83	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB' × R) ℂ)
    84	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    85	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)) )
    86	
    87	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    88	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    89	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    93	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    94	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    95	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    96	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    97	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    98	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    99	    (fun p =>
   100	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
   101	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
   102	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
   103	
   104	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   105	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   107	-/
   108	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   109	  (.pauli W, 0)
   110	
   111	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
   112	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
   113	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
   114	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   117	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   118	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   119	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   120	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   121	  fun p q =>
   122	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   123	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   124	    else 0
   125	
   126	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
   127	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   128	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   129	-/
   130	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   131	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   132	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   133	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   134	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   135	  fun p q =>
   136	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   137	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   138	    else 0
   139	
   140	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   141	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   142	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   145	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   146	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   147	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   148	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   149	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   150	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   151	  fun p q =>
   152	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   153	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   154	    else 0
   155	
   156	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   157	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   158	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   159	-/
   160	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   161	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   162	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   163	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   164	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   165	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   166	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   167	  fun p q =>
   168	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   169	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   170	    else 0
   171	
   172	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   173	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   174	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   175	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   176	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   177	-/
   178	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   179	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   180	  ιA' : Type
   181	  ιB' : Type
   182	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   183	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   184	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   185	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   186	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   187	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   188	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   189	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   190	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   191	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   192	
   193	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   194	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   195	
   196	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   197	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   198	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   199	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   200	-/
   201	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   202	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   203	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   204	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   205	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   206	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   207	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   208	
   209	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   210	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   212	-/
   213	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   214	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   215	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   216	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   217	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   218	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   219	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   220	
   221	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   222	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   223	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   224	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   225	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   226	Blueprint
   227	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   228	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   229	
   230	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   231	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   232	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   233	-/
   234	theorem pauli_soundness :
   235	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   236	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   237	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   238	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   239	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   240	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   241	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   242	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   243	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   244	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   245	  sorry
   246	
   247	end
   248	
   249	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   207	/-- The type-4 projection retaining `V_X`, `V_Z`, `V_{R_X}`, and `V_{R_Z}` from

   211	def pauliSharedProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliSpace P :=
   212	  fun i => match i with

   214	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))))
   215	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
   216	  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   217	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   218	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())
   219	
   220	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   221	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
   222	and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the
   223	shared projection has level 1.  Blueprint
   224	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   225	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   226	-/
   227	def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
   228	  | .point _ => 1
   229	  | .aline _ => 2
   230	  | .dline _ => 3
   231	  | .pauli _ => 0
   232	  | .pairW _ => 1
   233	  | .pair => 1
   234	  | .ms _ => 1
   235	
   236	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   237	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   238	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
   239	is the direct finite-space form of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   240	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   241	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   242	-/
   243	noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   244	    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
   245	  match t with
   246	  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   247	  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   248	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   249	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   250	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   251	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   252	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection
   253	
   254	/-- Level assertions for the typed Pauli CL maps.  These are Lean-only
   255	proof obligations corresponding to the prose following `def:pauli-question-distribution`
   256	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   257	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   258	-/
   259	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   260	    IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ (pauliCLLevel t) (pauliCL P t) := by
   261	  sorry
   262	
   263	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   264	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   265	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   266	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   267	-/
   268	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   269	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   270	  let lineEdges :=
   271	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   272	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   273	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   277	  let basisEdges :=
   278	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   279	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   280	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   281	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   282	  let pairEdges :=
   283	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   284	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   285	  let msEdges' :=
   286	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   287	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   288	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   289	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   290	
   291	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   292	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   293	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   294	-/
   295	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   296	
   297	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   298	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   299	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   302	-/
   303	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   304	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   305	
   306	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   307	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   308	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   309	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   310	-/
   311	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   312	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   313	  simp [pauliEdges]
   314	
   315	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   316	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   317	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   318	-/
   319	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   320	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   321	  by
   322	    classical
   323	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   324	    exact
   325	      Distribution.map
   326	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   327	        (fun s =>
   328	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   329	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   330	
   331	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   332	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   333	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   334	-/
   335	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   336	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   337	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   338	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   339	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   340	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   341	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   342	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   343	  deriving DecidableEq
   344	
   345	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   346	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   347	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   348	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   349	-/
   350	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   351	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   352	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   353	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   354	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   355	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   356	
   357	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   358	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   359	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   360	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

     4	/-!
     5	# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
     6	
     7	This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
     8	states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
     9	`Measurement` structure.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
    14	`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	/--
    27	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    28	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
    31	-/
    32	structure Game where
    33	  QuestionA : Type
    34	  QuestionB : Type
    35	  AnswerA : Type
    36	  AnswerB : Type
    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    38	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    39	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    40	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    41	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    42	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    43	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    44	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
    45	  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
    46	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    47	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    48	
    49	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    50	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    51	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    52	
    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    57	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    64	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    65	
    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    67	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    68	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    69	-/
    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd
    75	
    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152	
   153	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     5	
     6	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     7	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     8	estimates to later proof stages.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    23	
    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    38	-/
    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    45	
    46	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

520	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   521	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   522	-/
   523	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   524	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   525	  open Classical in
   526	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   527	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   528	      if tA = tB then
   529	        decide (a = b)
   530	      else
   531	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   532	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   533	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   534	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   535	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   536	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   538	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   539	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   540	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   541	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   542	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   543	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   544	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   545	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   546	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   547	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   548	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   550	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   552	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   553	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   554	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   555	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   556	          else true
   557	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   567	    else false
   568	
   569	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   570	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   571	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   572	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   573	-/
   574	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   575	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   576	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   577	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   578	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   579	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   580	  μ_prob := by sorry
   581	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   582	
   583	end
   584	
   585	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

360	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   361	-/
   362	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   363	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   364	  toFun
   365	    | .value a => .inl a
   366	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   367	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   368	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   369	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))

1	\section{Classical and Quantum Low-degree Tests}
     2	\label{sec:ldt}
     3	
     4	In this section we introduce the classical and quantum low individual degree tests, that form the basis of our classical, quantum-sound and quantum PCP constructions. For quantum soundness of the classical test we refer to~\cite{ML20}. For the quantum test, we refer to~\cite{natarajan2018low} and its adaptation to the low individual degree test given in Appendix~\ref{sec:qld-analysis}. 
     5	The protocol in this work combines both of these tests, using the quantum
     6	low individual degree test for question reduction and the classical low individual degree test for
     7	answer reduction.
     8	Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier} below introduces the classical test,
     9	and Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier} does the same for the quantum 
    10	test.
    11	Prior to doing this, we introduce the \emph{Magic Square game} in
    12	Section~\ref{sec:ms}, a key subroutine in the quantum test.
    13	
    14	
    15	\subsection{The classical low-degree test}
    16	\label{sec:ld-verifier}
    17	
    18	We begin with a generalization of the classical low-degree test known as the
    19	``simultaneous individual low-degree test''.
    20	We sometimes refer to this as the ``classical low-degree test'' for short.
    21	The low-degree test is used as a subroutine in the Pauli Basis test (see
    22	Section~\ref{sec:pauli-verifier}) as well as the answer-reduction normal form
    23	verifier (see Section~\ref{sec:ans}).
    24	We describe the test as a nonlocal game in Section~\ref{sec:ld-game} and show
    25	that the question distribution can be implemented as a (typed) conditionally
    26	linear distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL
    27	distributions).
    28	
    29	
    30	\subsubsection{The game}
    31	\label{sec:ld-game}
    32	
    33	The game $\game^\ld$ is parametrized by a tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
    34	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
    35	and $m$ divides $q$.
    36	We sometimes write $\game^\ld_\ldparams$ to emphasize the dependence of the
    37	classical low-degree test on the parameter tuple $\ldparams$.
    38	
    39	We first provide a high-level description of the game for $k=1$.
    40	It is based on the low-individual degree variant of the multilinearity test
    41	of~\cite{babai1991non}, where one player (called the ``points player'') receives
    42	a random point $u \in \F_q^m$, and the other player (called the ``lines
    43	player'') receives a random axis-parallel line $\line$ that contains $u$, i.e.\
    44	the line parallel to the $i$-th axis which goes through point $u$, for uniformly
    45	random $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$.
    46	The points player is supposed to respond with a value $a \in \F_q$, and the
    47	lines player is supposed to respond with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of
    48	degree at most $d$ such that $f_\line(u_i) = a$, where $u_i$ is the $i$-th
    49	coordinate of $u$.
    50	
    51	Suppose the players agree beforehand on a global polynomial $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$
    52	such that every variable has degree at most $d$.
    53	Then a winning strategy is the following: the points player responds with
    54	$g(u)$, and the lines player responds with the univariate polynomial $f_\line$
    55	that is the restriction of $g$ to line $\line$; formally, for $t \in \F_q$,
    56	\[f_\line(t)=g(u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_{i-1},t,u_{i+1},\ldots,u_m)\;.\] It is easy to
    57	see that $f_\line(t)$ has degree at most $d$ in the variable $t$.
    58	Thus in this case the players will pass the low-degree test with probability
    59	$1$.
    60	The low-degree testing theorem states that the converse approximately holds: if
    61	the players pass the low-degree test with probability close to $1$, then their
    62	responses must be approximately consistent (in some sense) with a global
    63	polynomial $g$ with individual degree $d$.
    64	
    65	When $k > 1$, the players are supposed to respond with a \emph{tuple} of
    66	answers; and the test is intended to check that the players' responses are
    67	consistent with a $k$-tuple of functions $g_i: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ that are
    68	polynomials where every variable has degree at most $d$.
    69	
    70	The game that we use is slightly more elaborate than the ``axis-parallel
    71	lines-versus-points'' test just described.
    72	In addition, we have two other subtests.
    73	One is a ``diagonal line-vs-points'' test: here, the points player receives a
    74	point $u \in \F_q^m$ as before, but the lines player receives a line $\line$
    75	that goes through $u$ but is not necessarily axis-aligned.
    76	Instead, it's chosen by first picking an index $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$
    77	uniformly at random, picking $v \in \F_q^m$ uniformly at random, and letting $v'
    78	= \pi_{i-1}(v) = (0,0,\ldots,0,v_i,v_{i+1},\ldots,v_m)$ (i.e., $\pi_{i-1}$
    79	zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of its input).
    80	Then, the line is defined as the set
    81	\[
    82		\line = \{ u + tv' : t \in \F_q \}\;,
    83	\]
    84	which is a uniformly random line in the affine subspace of $\F^m_q$
    85	corresponding to all points $v$ whose first $(i-1)$ coordinates match those of
    86	$u$.
    87	The points player responds with a value $a \in \F_q$, the lines player responds
    88	with a univariate polynomial $f_\line$ of degree $md$,\footnote{Since $\line$ is
    89	  no longer axis-parallel, the restriction of an individual degree-$d$
    90	  polynomial $g$ to a line $\line$ may yield a degree $md$ polynomial.}
    91	and the verifier checks that $f_\line(t_u) = a$ (where $t_u \in \F_q$ is the
    92	projection of $u$ onto the line $\line$ with respect to a canonical
    93	parameterization of $\line$).
    94	
    95	The other additional test is a ``consistency test'', where both players receive
    96	either the same points question, the same axis-parallel lines question, or the
    97	same diagonal lines question.
    98	In all cases they are expected to respond with the same answer.
    99	
   100	
   101	
   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}
   175	
   176	
   177	
   178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.
   238	
   239	
   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

   320	\paragraph{Decision procedure} The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the
   321	game $\game^\ld$ is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}.
   322	The table at the top specifies a parsing scheme for the questions and answers,
   323	depending on the type of question.
   324	For example, when a player receives a question with type $\Point$, the question
   325	content $x$, a bit string of length $m \log q$, should be interpreted by the
   326	decision procedure and the players as an element of the vector space $\F_q^m$,
   327	as indicated in Section~\ref{sec:ff-representations}.
   328	Similarly the answer to a question with type $\Point$ is expected to be a bit
   329	string of length $\ldc \log q$, and is interpreted as an element of $\F_q^\ldc$.
   330	For questions with type $\ALine$, the question content is a $(m \log q + \log
   331	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a pair $(u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$,
   332	which in turn can be interpreted as a specification for an axis-parallel line
   333	$\line(u_0,e_i)$ in $\F_q^m$ where $i = \chi(s)$, as described in
   334	\Cref{lem:alnf}.
   335	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$d$ univariate
   336	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,e_i)$, each polynomial given by a
   337	list of $d+1$ coefficients.
   338	For questions with type $\DLine$, the question content is a $(2m \log q + \log
   339	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a triple $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q
   340	\times \F_q^m$ that specifies a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ where $v' =
   341	\pi_{i-1}(v)$ as described in \Cref{lem:dlnf}.
   342	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$md$ univariate
   343	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,v')$.
   344	If the answers returned by the players do not fit this format the decision
   345	procedure rejects.

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.

   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
